pr_title: Replace ISystemClock with TimeProvider in Kestrel
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/47472
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/13628

This replaces the internal ISystemClock types with the new TimeProvider abstraction. I also included https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/13628 which switches most operations to timestamps instead of utc dates, which may clean up the code a bit and allow for other micro-optimizations by working more directly with longs than DateTimeOffset.

Fixes #37862 (quarantined test which hasn't failed in 30+ days)

review_comments: Should the AdvanceTo calls check that the time doesn't go backwards?
Backwards is fine, except if you make the timestamp go negative. We could check for that.

Why is backwards fine? Especially when `_timestamp` can be initialized to 0 randomly, meaning it could become negative.
`_timestamp = Random.Shared.NextInt64(0, System.GetTimestamp() * 100);`
Right, that's why I added a check for negative _timestamp and _utcTicks.

That makes it worse. Because now a test will be flaky if it does any sort of time reversing.

And I still haven't seen a scenario where we do want to go backwards. So why let that happen until such a scenario occurs?
Hmmm that's a good point about flakyness. I'll see if preventing reversals causes any issues.
This is only called by tests, right? Can we move this to the `MockTimeProvider`?

Nit:

```suggestion
    private static long GetTimestamp(this TimeProvider timeProvider, long timeStamp, TimeSpan timeSpan)
```
? This is used by Http2Connection and several tests.
